lines.en: scene black
: Rin, are you in there?
lines.zh: : Rin，你在里面吗？

lines.en: : It's time for your scene commentary.
lines.zh: : 你的场景解说时间到了。

lines.en: There's no answer. And considering I have already played this event, I'm stricken with a very bad feeling about what's to come...
lines.zh: 没有人回答。而考虑到我已经玩过这个事件，我对接下来要发生什么有种非常不好的预感……

lines.en: scene rinisfine1 with flash
But that's okay because I just remembered I'm not the one who handles the commentary for these. Selebus is.
lines.zh: 不过没关系，因为我刚想起来，负责这些解说的人不是我。是 Selebus。

lines.en: : Here is my name so you can understand that the narrator is now changing.
lines.zh: : 这是我的名字，好让你知道叙述者正在换人。

lines.en: Delirium, without beating around the bush, is probably the first scene in this game that I ever really {i}tried{/i} with.
lines.zh: 《谵妄》—— 不绕弯子地说 —— 大概是我在这游戏里第一次真正{i}用心去做{/i}的场景。

lines.en: That's less true now for any player who's gone through the revamped version and gotten to experience higher production quality across the board-
lines.zh: 对于玩过重制版、体验到整体更高制作水准的玩家来说，这点现在没那么明显了 ——

lines.en: But before such a thing existed, the early game in Lessons in Love was half-baked, half-hearted, and nothing more than a way for me to test the waters and try out a new medium.
lines.zh: 但在那之前，《Lessons in Love》的早期内容做得很潦草、也很敷衍，无非是我拿来试水、试新媒介的方式。

lines.en: You see (And this is a bit tangential, so bear with me), I'd worked on visual novels in the past- but never a Western-feeling one with sandboxy elements dumped into it.
lines.zh: 你看（这段有点跑题，忍一下），我以前做过视觉小说 —— 但从没做过一款西式感觉的、还往里塞了沙盒元素的。

lines.en: And considering I never had much interest in Western visual novels in the first place, I had a hard time {i}seriously{/i} writing a game I didn't take seriously myself.
lines.zh: 而考虑到我本来就不太喜欢西式视觉小说，我很难{i}认真{/i}地去写一款我自己都不当回事的游戏。

lines.en: Delirium was the first {i}real{/i} exception to that.
lines.zh: 《谵妄》是第一个{i}真正{/i}的例外。

lines.en: It was a scene where I could take experiences from my own life and implant them into a character who carried that part of me with them.
lines.zh: 那是一个我可以把自己人生里的经历拿出来、移植到某个角色身上的场景，让那个角色替我带着那一部分。

lines.en: It was a way for me to speak to all of you in a manner that transcends opaque text boxes and line after line of amateurish code, for I am not an expert when it comes to computers-
lines.zh: 那是我用来和你们所有人说话的一种方式 —— 一种超越了不透明文本框、超越了一行行外行代码的方式，因为在电脑这件事上我算不上专家 ——

lines.en: But I am an expert when it comes to feeling like this gigantic orb we live on is littered with nothing but filler.
lines.zh: 但在「觉得我们住的这颗巨大球体上面除了填充物什么都没有」这件事上，我是专家。

lines.en: I am an expert when it comes to forgetting to eat or shower or sleep or {i}think{/i} because there is something inside of me that forces me to just sit there sometimes.
lines.zh: 在忘记吃饭、洗澡、睡觉、甚至是{i}思考{/i}这件事上，我是专家 —— 因为我体内有某种东西，有时会强迫我就那么坐着。

lines.en: It's not romantic. It's not inspiring. But it's real and it's who I am and, for a brief moment in time, I {i}remembered{/i} that while making this game.
lines.zh: 这一点都不浪漫。也不励志。但它是真实的，是我本人，而且在制作这游戏的某个短暂时刻，我{i}记起了{/i}这一点。

lines.en: And I wanted to share it with you since it's the only thing I really {i}know{/i} at the end of the day.
lines.zh: 而我想把它分享给你们，因为说到底，这是我唯一真正{i}懂{/i}的东西。

lines.en: The scene begins with Sensei entering Rin's room, fully aware that she hasn't been feeling {i}right{/i} as of late but, without knowing her bad habits, isn't sure what to expect.
lines.zh: 场景开头，Sensei 走进 Rin 的房间。他完全知道她最近状态{i}不对{/i}，但因为不了解她的那些坏习惯，也不确定会看到什么。

lines.en: What he's greeted with is the sight of a girl he's in the early stages of learning to care about {i}suffering{/i} while he's left scrambling and trying to figure out what to do.
lines.zh: 迎接他的，是一个他才刚开始学着在乎的女孩正在{i}受苦{/i}的画面，而他只能手忙脚乱地想办法。

lines.en: He didn't come here with the expectation of force-feeding hope back into a teenage girl. In fact, at this point in the game, if he knew that's what he'd be getting into, he'd probably just stay away.
lines.zh: 他来这儿，并不是打算把希望硬塞回一个少女的身体里。事实上，在游戏这个阶段，如果他知道自己要面对的是这个，他大概会直接躲开。

lines.en: But you, the player, in an attempt to get either further into the story or further into Rin's pants, {i}did.{/i}
lines.zh: 但你，玩家，为了把故事推得更深、或者把 Rin 的裤子脱得更透，{i}还是来了{/i}。

lines.en: {i}You{/i} showed up here, which meant {i}you{/i} would now have to come face to face with the fact that life is not all fun and sex and anime girls who wear basketball shorts to bed.
lines.zh: {i}你{/i}出现在了这里，也就意味着{i}你{/i}现在必须直面一个事实：人生不全是乐子、性、还有穿着篮球短裤睡觉的动画少女。

lines.en: It's a place where, sometimes, shitty things happen to people for no good reason other than the fact that they got dealt a bad hand.
lines.zh: 这是一个有时候烂事就会发生在人身上、而且根本没什么像样理由的地方 —— 唯一的理由就是他们拿到了一手烂牌。

lines.en: Fortunately, Rin's hand wasn't as bad as it could have been. Other people have been through worse. (This is what your friends will tell you when you try to explain why you didn't show up last night.)
lines.zh: 好在 Rin 的牌还没烂到不能再烂。还有人经历过更糟的。（这句是你试图解释昨晚为什么没出现时，朋友们会说的话。）

lines.en: And fortunately, this is just a trial from God...and she's only experiencing it because God knows she can handle it. (This one comes from the church.)
lines.zh: 而且好在，这只是来自上帝的一场试炼……她之所以会经历，是因为上帝知道她扛得住。（这句来自教会。）

lines.en: She's brave! She's strong! (This one's from your mother.)
lines.zh: 她很勇敢！她很坚强！（这句来自你妈妈。）

lines.en: She's just going through a phase! (Your father.)
lines.zh: 她只是在经历一个阶段而已！（你爸爸。）

lines.en: She needs help. (Someone they paid to say that.)
lines.zh: 她需要帮助。（这句出自某个他们花钱请来的人。）

lines.en: scene frown with flash
{b}BUT NONE OF THEM GET IT.{/b}
lines.zh: {b}但他们没有一个真的懂。{/b}

lines.en: And the sad truth is that none of them ever will.
lines.zh: 而悲哀的真相是，他们永远也不会懂。

lines.en: There are little capsules you can swallow that are meant to numb the pain, but when everything feels numb to begin with, what's even the point?
lines.zh: 有那种可以吞下去的小胶囊，本意是麻痹痛苦，但如果一切从一开始就已经是麻木的，那又有什么意义？

lines.en: I'm glad you walked into her room because it meant you got to experience one of the only scenes in Lessons in Love that can be taken no more than two ways.
lines.zh: 我很高兴你走进了她的房间，因为这意味着你体验到了《Lessons in Love》里为数不多、只能有两种解读的场景之一。

lines.en: Either you get it...or you don't.
lines.zh: 要么你懂……要么你不懂。

lines.en: That's it.
lines.zh: 就这些。

lines.en: scene rinisfine16r with flash
I was tired of seeing different forms of media romanticizating the disgusting, sickening, and entirely unattractive disorder that is depression.
lines.zh: 我看腻了各种媒介把「抑郁」这种恶心、令人作呕、毫无美感的疾病浪漫化。

lines.en: I was tired of people pretending to understand things they {i}don't.{/i} Tired of the textbook definitions and make-believe depictions of something that is different for {i}everyone.{/i}
lines.zh: 我厌倦了人们装作懂那些他们{i}根本不懂{/i}的东西。厌倦了教科书式的定义，以及把一件对{i}每个人{/i}都不一样的事，描绘得像假的一样。

lines.en: But when you try to talk about things like this in real-life, you're bombarded by know-it-alls who try to explain your feelings for you because you're simply incapable of doing it yourself.
lines.zh: 可当你想在现实里谈这种事，就会被一堆万事通围攻，他们抢着替你解释你的感受，理由是你自己根本做不到。

lines.en: There's no way {i}you{/i} can come to terms with the underlying emptiness in all things. You're far too...empty. Aren't you? You need someone to do it for you. It only makes sense.
lines.zh: {i}你{/i}怎么可能真正接受万事万物之下那层空虚呢。你太……空了。不是吗？你需要有人替你做这件事。这才说得通啊。

lines.en: Take this with water twice a day after a meal. If that doesn't work, take this instead. Now this. Now all of them.
lines.zh: 这个饭后配水服，一天两次。不行就换这个。再换这个。现在全都一起上。

lines.en: scene frown with flash
{b}WHY AREN'T YOU FIXED YET?{/b}
lines.zh: {b}你怎么还没被修好？{/b}

lines.en: scene rinisfine16r with flash
Rin is not a textbook depiction of depression.
lines.zh: Rin 不是一个教科书式的抑郁样本。

lines.en: She's not a character who only has it to emphasize her {i}better{/i} qualities by contrast.
lines.zh: 她也不是那种靠得病来反衬自己{i}更好{/i}一面的角色。

lines.en: It's not a tool meant to make you {i}love{/i} her.
lines.zh: 这也不是一个用来让你{i}爱上{/i}她的工具。

lines.en: It's just something she has.
lines.zh: 这只是她身上有的东西。

lines.en: And this is what that looks like sometimes.
lines.zh: 而有时候，它就是长这样。

lines.en: The point of Delirium was forcing people to come face to face with a darker side of reality, not beseeching them to change it.
lines.zh: 《谵妄》的重点是逼人们去直面现实更黑暗的一面，而不是恳求他们去改变它。

lines.en: If you came out of the scene wanting to {i}help{/i} Rin, you missed that point entirely.
lines.zh: 如果你看完这场戏之后想的是要{i}帮{/i} Rin，那你完全没抓到重点。

lines.en: She does not {i}need{/i} to be helped. At least not in the way you think she does.
lines.zh: 她并不{i}需要{/i}被帮助。至少不是你以为的那种方式。

lines.en: She needs to be {i}accepted.{/i}
lines.zh: 她需要的是被{i}接纳{/i}。

lines.en: We all do.
lines.zh: 我们都需要。

lines.en: So to those of you out there who feel like Rin sometimes-
lines.zh: 所以，对那些有时也会像 Rin 一样感受的人 ——

lines.en: There is nothing wrong with feeling empty or hopeless, especially if those feelings are built into your brain.
lines.zh: 感到空虚或绝望并没有错，尤其当这些感受是被写进你大脑里的。

lines.en: If you want them to stop, there are options available to you. There's no guarantee they'll be successful, but you know they exist because you're not a fucking idiot.
lines.zh: 如果你想让它们停下来，你是有选择的。没人保证那些办法一定有效，但你知道它们存在，因为你他妈又不是白痴。

lines.en: Pay no mind to those who don't understand that- who toss the numbers of suicide hotlines at you like breadcrumbs to a fucking pigeon because they think you've never heard of Google.
lines.zh: 别去理会那些不懂这一点的人 —— 他们把自杀热线号码像给鸽子撒面包屑一样丢给你，只因为他们觉得你从没听说过 Google。

lines.en: They're just confused. And they're going to {i}remain{/i} confused if we don't get off of our fucking asses and teach them that we are {b}not{/b} broken.
lines.zh: 他们只是困惑而已。而如果我们不他妈从屁股上挪开、告诉他们我们{b}没有{/b}坏掉，他们就会{i}一直{/i}困惑下去。

lines.en: We're just different.
lines.zh: 我们只是不一样。

lines.en: I know it's hard and that it might even sound like I'm trying to do something about it as well with this hurried plea for semi-action...but I'm not.
lines.zh: 我知道这很难，而且我这段仓促的、半吊子的呼吁听起来甚至像是我也想为此做点什么……但我不是。

lines.en: I just want people to get it.
lines.zh: 我只是希望有人能懂。

lines.en: And I feel like no one ever does.
lines.zh: 而我感觉从来没有人懂。

lines.en: Delirium is a product of that neverending desire to be acknowledged as a human being and not a human being {i}with depression.{/i}
lines.zh: 《谵妄》正是那种无尽渴望的产物 —— 渴望被当作一个人来承认，而不是一个{i}有抑郁症的{/i}人。

lines.en: It is a love letter to those out there like me...and a metaphorical punch in the mouth to anyone who can see something like that and immediately think {i}she needs help.{/i}
lines.zh: 它是写给所有像我这样的人的一封情书……也是一记比喻意义上的、打在那些看到这种事就立刻想「{i}她需要帮助{/i}」的人嘴上的拳头。

lines.en: That is not for {i}you{/i} to decide.
lines.zh: 那不是由{i}你{/i}来决定的。

lines.en: So if you ever find yourself in the unfortunate position of walking into a room where someone is hurting, just {i}be{/i} with them. Or shit, leave them alone if they ask you to.
lines.zh: 所以，如果你哪天不幸走进一个有人正在痛苦的房间，那就只是{i}陪着{/i}他们。或者操，如果他们让你走开，那就走开。

lines.en: Just don't take it upon yourself to remind someone in the midst of their despair that they're not meant to feel that way.
lines.zh: 只是别自作主张地去提醒一个正处于绝望中的人：他们本不该有这种感受。

lines.en: They know.
lines.zh: 他们知道。

lines.en: scene black
Stop trying to save those who don't need saving.
lines.zh: 别再试着去拯救那些不需要被拯救的人。

lines.en: We might be starved, sleep-deprived and numb, but we're resilient fucking creatures.
lines.zh: 我们也许挨着饿、缺着觉、浑身麻木，但我们是他妈韧性很强的生物。

lines.en: And we just want to feel normal.
lines.zh: 而我们只是想感觉正常一点。

lines.en: We just want to feel pure.
lines.zh: 我们只是想感觉干净一点。

lines.en: scene meintheroom2 with flash
: It is at this point that I will, once again, answer several questions submitted by the audience.
lines.zh: : 到这个时候，我又要再一次回答观众提交的几个问题。

lines.en: : {b}Question 1:{/b} Delirium's role in developing Rin's character is obvious, but it's also an early humanizing event for Sensei...
lines.zh: : {b}问题一：{/b}《谵妄》在塑造 Rin 这个角色上的作用很明显，但它同时也是 Sensei 早期的一次「人性化」事件……

lines.en: : Could you talk about how it fits into your goals for his chapter one arc?
lines.zh: : 能说说它如何贴合你对他第一章弧线的目标吗？

lines.en: : I can!
lines.zh: : 我可以！

lines.en: : Chapter One Sensei is a fucking prick. So is Chapter Two Sensei and Chapter Three Sensei as well, but Chapter One Sensei is a whole different breed.
lines.zh: : 第一章的 Sensei 是个彻头彻尾的混蛋。第二章、第三章的 Sensei 也是，但第一章的 Sensei 完全是另一个品种。

lines.en: : In essence, he's a lot like the player- someone who only cares about the girls on a surface level because they're attractive and he wants to fuck them.
lines.zh: : 本质上，他和玩家很像 —— 只在表面上在乎这些女孩，因为她们好看，而他想操她们。

lines.en: : Delirium, as mentioned in regard to the way I wanted players to feel earlier, slaps him across the face with the realization that the girls are {i}more{/i} than that.
lines.zh: : 《谵妄》—— 就像我前面说希望玩家感受到的那样 —— 一巴掌扇在他脸上，让他意识到这些女孩{i}不止{/i}于此。

lines.en: : He sees someone enduring a great deal of pain and, as someone who has endured a great deal of pain himself (Even if it's suppressed at the time), he's forced to think differently.
lines.zh: : 他看到有人正在承受巨大的痛苦，而他自己也承受过巨大的痛苦（尽管当时被压了下去），于是他被迫换一种方式思考。

lines.en: : It's a rare moment of humanization because he is forced to come to terms with the fact that he is not the {i}only{/i} human being out there.
lines.zh: : 这是难得的人性化时刻，因为他被迫接受一个事实：他并不是这世上{i}唯一的{/i}人。

lines.en: : Chapter One is filled with many of these small moments.
lines.zh: : 第一章里充满了许多这样的小瞬间。

lines.en: : And while Delirium may be the first of these you encounter based on play order, its overall place in slowly building up an actual {i}character{/i} inside a shell of a man remains strong to this day.
lines.zh: : 而且虽然按游玩顺序来说，《谵妄》可能是你最先遇到的一个，但它在这个「空壳男人」内部慢慢堆出一个真正的{i}角色{/i}这件事上的地位，到今天依然很强。

lines.en: : {b}Question 2:{/b} Did you consider having this first encounter with Rin’s issues be even more shocking than it is currently?
lines.zh: : {b}问题二：{/b}你有没有想过，让这场与 Rin 的问题的初次相遇比现在更震撼？

lines.en: : Absolutely not. Converting a major part of my life into nothing more than a tool for shock value sounds utterly disgusting to me.
lines.zh: : 绝对没有。把我人生里这么重要的一部分，变成纯粹用来博眼球的工具，这听起来让我恶心透了。

lines.en: : The goal of Delirium was never to {i}shock{/i} anyone- it was to get people to keep their eyes open and accept the many impurities this life has to offer rather than just ignoring them.
lines.zh: : 《谵妄》的目标从来不是要{i}震撼{/i}谁 —— 而是让人们睁着眼睛，去接受这人生不得不提供的那些杂质，而不是直接无视它们。

lines.en: : I talked about it before, but I am tired of games and movies and TV shows that make every single case of depression into something earth-shattering when that's really not how it is in day to day life.
lines.zh: : 我说过了，我厌倦了游戏、电影、电视剧把每一个抑郁的例子都拍成惊天动地的样子，而在日常生活里根本不是那样。

lines.en: : You can have depression without wanting to kill yourself. You can have depression without accidentally overdosing on medication to try and {i}make it stop.{/i}
lines.zh: : 你可以有抑郁症，但并不想自杀。你可以有抑郁症，但不会因为想{i}让它停下{/i}而意外服药过量。

lines.en: : You can function like a normal human being because {i}you are a normal human being.{/i}
lines.zh: : 你可以像一个正常人一样运转，因为{i}你本来就是一个正常人{/i}。

lines.en: : I wouldn't have been able to sleep at night if I had blown it out of proportion by turning it into something bigger when it was never meant to be.
lines.zh: : 如果我把它夸张成某种本来不该是的、更大的东西，我晚上会睡不着觉的。

lines.en: : {b}Question 3:{/b} Was the revamp of the scene changed so that it fits into your goal better?
lines.zh: : {b}问题三：{/b}这场戏的重制是为了更贴合你的目标吗？

lines.en: : Not really. I just got better at writing and found a lot of the old text to be kind of cringeworthy by comparison. That's really all there is to say about that.
lines.zh: : 也不全是。我只是写得更好了，觉得不少旧文本相比之下有点尴尬。这事真的就只有这些可说。

lines.en: : {b}Question 4:{/b} Did how close you are to Rin and your proximity to the topic in delirium make this event harder or easier to write?
lines.zh: : {b}问题四：{/b}你和 Rin 的亲近程度、以及你离《谵妄》这个主题的近距离，让这个事件更好写还是更难写？

lines.en: : A little of both, actually. Mental health, as a whole, is a tough topic to write about as the wrong word choice can often make it sound like you're arguing the opposite of your point.
lines.zh: : 其实两者都有。心理健康整体来说是个很难写的主题，因为选错一个词，常常就会让它听起来像是在反驳你自己的论点。

lines.en: : This commentary alone is a good example of that. It's taken me probably twice as long as the others have but, at the same time, it {i}feels{/i} shorter as it's something I'm passionate about.
lines.zh: : 光是这篇解说就是个好例子。它花的时间大概是其他篇的两倍，但同时它{i}感觉{/i}更短 —— 因为这是我真正有热情的东西。

lines.en: : The scene itself worked the same way. It took longer and had more work put into it, but it was easier on me mentally as it's something I know very well.
lines.zh: : 那场戏本身也是这样。它花的时间更长、投入的功夫更多，但在精神上对我更轻松，因为这是我非常熟悉的东西。

lines.en: : {b}Final Question:{/b} How was the community reaction to Delirium at the time of its release? Was it encouraging?
lines.zh: : {b}最后一个问题：{/b}《谵妄》发布时玩家社区的反响如何？有给你鼓励吗？

lines.en: : I honestly don't remember much about the initial reaction to Delirium as it happened {i}very{/i} early on in Lessons in Love and the community was just...significantly smaller than it is now.
lines.zh: : 说实话，我不太记得《谵妄》最初的反响 —— 因为它发生在《Lessons in Love》很早很早的时候，当时的社区规模……比现在小得多。

lines.en: : But I will say that, to this day, the overall reaction to it is still not quite what I wanted it to be in that many people are walking away from it with the wrong idea.
lines.zh: : 但我要说的是，直到今天，它的整体反响仍然不完全是我想要的那样 —— 因为很多人看完之后带走的是错误的理解。

lines.en: : That does not, however, change the near hundreds of people who have reached out to me after playing that scene to thank me for my raw and honest depiction of depression.
lines.zh: : 但这并不影响那近几百个人 —— 他们玩完那场戏后联系我，感谢我对抑郁那种不加修饰、诚实的刻画。

lines.en: : Being able to reach people like me in a way that helps them feel more human is the greatest accomplishment I could have made as a writer, and I thank every single of you for sharing your stories.
lines.zh: : 能够触达像我这样的人、让他们觉得自己更像一个人，这是我作为作家能取得的最大成就。也谢谢你们每一个人，愿意分享自己的故事。

lines.en: : So even if there are people who continue to misunderstand, I will not. I know what it is like. And I will continue to share my experiences and hope that they can reach others.
lines.zh: : 所以，即便有人继续误解，我也不会。我知道那是什么滋味。而我会继续分享我的经历，希望它们能触达其他人。

lines.en: scene black
Thank you for taking the time out of your day to read the scene commentary for Rin Rokuhara’s event, “Delirium.”
lines.zh: 感谢你抽出时间阅读 Rin Rokuhara 事件《谵妄》的场景解说。

lines.en: Stick around and continue showing your support for more scenes just like this in the future.
lines.zh: 请继续关注，并继续支持未来更多像这样的场景。

lines.en: Selebus, signing off.
lines.zh: Selebus，下线。
